messages:
owen: hey @devex — running into a CI flake in rb-sdk sampleapp on windows gha after bumping Faraday. Local `bundle exec rake` passes. Anyone seen this?
jess: saw a Windows bundler path thing last week. can you paste the failing log?
owen: failing test is `test_auth_retry.rb` — GH log snippet:
```
FATAL: LoadError: cannot load such file -- win32/some_native
16:22:11 /home/runner/work/myrepo/test/test_auth_retry.rb:14
```
tai: hmmmm looks like a native ext pulled in via dependency. try `bundle lock --add-platform x86_64-mingw32` or pin the transitive gem. which faraday version did you bump to?
owen: faraday 2.8.0 -> 2.9.0. suspect multipart-post or similar pulled in native. tests only fail on windows-latest.
maya: we could also force a pure-ruby adapter in CI for the matrix job as a short term. e.g. add `gem "multipart-post", "~> 2.1"` or vendor the tiny helper.
jess: also FYI re: retry/auth parity — ruby's default retry backoff is linear while go/external libs we use tend to be exponential. unrelated to load error but worth adding a unit to lock behavior so we don't regress.
owen: good call. how do folks usually repro windows locally?
tai: use `act` or run a Windows runner VM, or emulate by adding the platform and running locally: `bundle lock --add-platform x86_64-mingw32 && bundle install --local --deployment` then `ruby -Ilib test/test_auth_retry.rb`. that usually catches native load issues.
owen: thanks. I'll open a small PR pinning multipart-post and add the lockfile platform. will also add the retry unit test.
sam: I can review the PR, please keep the change minimal and include a one-line changelog and an entry in CONTRIBUTING about reproducing Windows CI.
devex-bot: Troubleshooting guide: https://redwood-internal.devex/ci-windows#native-gems
owen: dropping a draft PR now: #2482 — linux tests green, windows queued for rerun. will update with results.
maya: :thumbsup: if windows rerun still flakes, add a skip for that test on Windows and file a follow-up issue to remove the skip after upstream fix.
jess: also add a tiny assertion for retry backoff e.g. `assert_equal expected_backoff, client.retry_policy.backoff(2)` so we keep parity.
owen: good notes, will include both the platform lock and the backoff unit. thanks everyone!
